summary: Implemented the baseline CI foundation locally (HD-0013): .github/workflows/ci.yml (push to claude/** and claude-dev, pull_request into claude-dev and main; contents: read only; no secrets, environments, caches or deployment; actions pinned to full commit SHAs that were read and checked in the actions' own repositories; install without scripts; lint, tsc, ops:validate, ops:test, build), a policy.workflow_policy section and schema (policy 0.3.0), a restricted YAML reader, and a deterministic allow-list workflow-safety checker that npm run ops:validate now runs, with validator floors that the policy file alone cannot lower. 168 new tests introduce unsafe configurations and expect rejection (suite: 353, from 185); 35 rules were mutation-checked. All five required checks pass, a local simulation of the exact workflow steps passes with no credential in the environment, and the production build output matches the baseline. Documentation: ADR-0011, CI architecture, activation guide, OPS-0003 proposal, OQ-0034. Nothing was pushed or activated; no GitHub setting was changed; the Reel work is untouched.

risk.rationale: The work adds a workflow (.github/**), changes ops/, the policy and a schema, all control-plane paths that policy classes as B, plus governed project memory. No class C path was touched, no website file changed, and nothing was activated.

deviations.description: Added policy.workflow_policy, its schema section and a policy version bump to 0.3.0, added REQ-OPS-010 and HD-0013, added two ops libraries to memory_contract.required_files, and added .github to the content-scan roots.
deviations.reason: The checker must read the approved workflow shape from a human-owned file, and the instruction allowed policy and schema changes where necessary and within scope; the new requirement and decision record the instruction itself.

deviations.description: The checker enforces an allow-list with a restricted YAML reader, not the line-based text checks the proposal described.
deviations.reason: Line-based checks could be evaded by YAML the file's own reader and GitHub's reader interpret differently; a reader that rejects ambiguous constructs removes that class of bypass. The proposal's own banner now records the difference.

deviations.description: The runner label is pinned to ubuntu-24.04 (the proposal said ubuntu-latest), setup-node's automatic caching is switched off explicitly, and the credential guard also covers an auth-token variable.
deviations.reason: A floating runner label changes behaviour silently; setup-node 7.1.0 enables dependency caching by default when package.json names npm as its package manager, which would add a cache that carries state between runs.

deviations.description: Chose actions/checkout and actions/setup-node as the GitHub-owned actions, and recorded them as approved in the policy under HD-0013.
deviations.reason: The instruction asked for actions pinned to verified SHAs but did not name them; these two are what the required steps (checkout, Node setup) need. The owner is asked to confirm the choice (OQ-0034).

deviations.description: Modified ops/tests/validate-memory.test.mjs and ops/tests/helpers.mjs: the ADR-count test no longer depends on how many ADRs exist, and the temporary copy used by tests includes .github.
deviations.reason: ADR-0011 broke an assumption in the existing test; the workflow files are now part of the validated tree.

deviations.description: Did not run any workflow linter or GitHub Actions run; a PyYAML cross-check and a local step-by-step simulation stand in.
deviations.reason: No push is authorised and no workflow linter is installed here; both limits are stated in the CI architecture and the activation guide.

unresolved_issues.description: The workflow has never run on GitHub. Whether GitHub accepts the file, how the hosted runner behaves, and whether the pinned actions run there are unobserved until an approved push (OQ-0028). Local simulation is not a substitute.

A pull request runs its own copy of the checker, so green CI is not evidence about changes to .github/, ops/, the policy or the schemas. Human review of those control-plane paths is the control until the trusted-base check proposed for OPS-0003 exists.

The repository's GitHub settings (approval for outside collaborators' workflow runs, default token permission, branch protection, whether the repository holds any secrets, the plan and account type) cannot be observed or set from here; they are recorded for the owner in OQ-0034 and OPS-0002-ACTIVATION.md.

Pushing claude/ops-0002-ci-baseline also publishes the nine OPS-0001 and OPS-0001B commits beneath it, and will probably start a hosting-service preview build of an unchanged site (the hosting settings are unobservable). Both are described in the activation guide.

Pinned labels age: ubuntu-24.04, Node 22 and the two action SHAs need reviewed updates; nothing updates them automatically. The installed ESLint version prints a deprecation notice during install (pre-existing, not changed).

The instruction to pin 'third-party and GitHub-owned actions' is read as allowing the two GitHub-owned actions the required steps need, and no third-party action.
Node 22 (the version used for every local check) is the right single version to test; the project's engines field only declares >= 18.18.
questions_for_human: OQ-0028: do you authorise a one-time push of claude/ops-0002-ci-baseline (which also publishes the nine earlier OPS-0001 and OPS-0001B commits under it, and may start a hosting preview build)? Without it the workflow cannot become active.

OQ-0034: will you set 'Require approval for all external contributors' for fork pull-request workflows, confirm the default workflow token is read-only, and after the first green run require the job named verify on claude-dev and main? Do you accept actions/checkout v7.0.1 and actions/setup-node v7.1.0, pinned as in the policy?
Merging into claude-dev later is a separate approval; note that the local claude-dev carries eight unpushed Reel commits, so it will diverge from a remote claude-dev that gains the OPS commits.
OQ-0023 (public or private repository for the longer term) and OQ-0020 (ratify the Phase 0 modifications and the ADRs) remain open; neither blocks OPS-0002.
Should the worktrees /home/user/m1pcs-ops-0001 and /home/user/m1pcs-ops-0002 be kept for review, or removed afterwards (the branches stay either way)?
